groups.summary: Made the first minute feel smaller. Took onboarding from an early prototype to a shipped, two-step flow.

moments.summary: Shared a quieter first pass at onboarding. One decision at a time.

sources.text:
First pass at the welcome flow. We were asking for five things before someone could try anything.

What if we start with just a name, then let them explore? Before and after below.

attachments.name: Before · everything at once
attachments.alt: Fictional onboarding form asking for several details.

attachments.name: After · just the first step
attachments.alt: Fictional welcome screen with a single name field.

moments.summary: Made the second step optional after Sam's feedback.

sources.text: This feels much better. Could the workspace step be skippable too? I'd love to see the product before naming the space.

moments.summary: Wrote down the principle so it survives this particular redesign.

sources.title: The first minute
sources.text:
Let people do something before asking them to configure everything.

A useful first action teaches the product better than a checklist. Ask for information when it becomes relevant, and let optional decisions stay optional.

moments.summary: Shipped the two-step welcome flow, including the skip we discussed.

sources.title: Make the first-run setup smaller
sources.text:
Ask for a name first. Move workspace settings to an optional second step.

Keeps entered values when going back and restores focus to the field that needs attention.

moments.summary: Scheduled a walkthrough to hear what still feels confusing.
Shared a few frames from the week. Less setup, more trying things.

sources.text: A small thing from this week: making the first minute feel like using the product, not filling in a form.
